clue.text: Meetings can be bits of noise, repeatedly in one case

indicators.note: the word is broken into bits and its letters put back together in another order

parts.note: the hissing S already in the word is given again and again, three more times

explanation.surface: Some meetings are nothing but racket, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one case' is a nod to the theme: one of the thirteen senators in the grid, Jeff Sessions of Alabama, shares this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sessions are periods when a court, legislature or group is assembled for business.

clue.text: Comfortable and efficient, and therefore with no amplification

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English
a mic (microphone) is what amplifies a voice

explanation.surface: Gear that is comfortable and efficient, and so needs no amplifier: an unplugged act, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design is shaped for the user's comfort and working efficiency.

clue.text: Mark scarcely half

indicators.note: only half of the next word is kept, the front four of its eight letters

explanation.surface: A mark that is barely there, hardly half visible.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark a healed wound leaves on the skin.

clue.text: Test of endurance or agreement

parts.note: a deal is an agreement between parties

explanation.surface: A choice between a gruelling trial and a negotiated settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful experience that has to be endured, a severe trial.

clue.text: Get ready to ride and slap dude senseless

indicators.note: something knocked senseless is in disorder, so these letters lose their arrangement

explanation.surface: A cowboy preparing to mount, and knocking some fellow out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To saddle up is to put the saddle on a horse before setting off on it.

clue.text: Tacos shredded in layers

indicators.note: food that is shredded is torn apart, so this word's letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A recipe note: tacos with the filling shredded and built up in layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coats of paint or icing are layers spread one over another.

clue.text: Songbird is very loud when held by string on top of church

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of what follows, so the pieces are joined in that order
what is held by something sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a chain is a string of linked things
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bird singing very loudly from a rope slung over a church roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string' suggests a violin or guitar, but here it is a run of linked things; ff is the score marking fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch known for its cheerful song.

clue.text: Beginning part of crucial phase

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the words that follow, lying within them

explanation.surface: The opening stage of some critical period.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, stands for the beginning, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Flushed up and in, without woodworking tools

indicators.note: in tells us this piece is placed inside the next

parts.note: sans is French for without, also used in English

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A worker red-faced and indoors because the tools have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks as if it belongs with the tools, but it is the French word English borrowed, holding the reversed colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanders are power tools that smooth wood with abrasive paper.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil to keep kosher is a remarkable thing

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a corer removes the cores from apples
K is a symbol printed on food packaging to certify it kosher

explanation.surface: A gadget for keeping a kitchen kosher is hailed as a wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A corker is informal for something or someone outstandingly good or astonishing.

clue.text: A groundbreaking alert

indicators.note: when something is breaking it falls to pieces, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An alert about something truly revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundbreaking' reads as one word meaning innovative; split it into 'ground' and 'breaking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on guard is watchful and ready for danger, as an alert person is.

clue.text: Showing no emotion, school official takes handheld device back

indicators.note: what a person takes in is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dean is a senior official in a school or college

indicators.note: back means the device's abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a PDA, personal digital assistant, is a handheld computer

explanation.surface: A stony-faced school official confiscates a pupil's gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan expression or delivery is deliberately blank and impassive.

clue.text: Rumpelstiltskin gleefully traps princess's father

indicators.note: the words that trap the answer hold it inside them

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale imp delights in ensnaring the royal father of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a king's daughter, so her father is a king, as in the Rumpelstiltskin tale.

clue.text: Evangelist's friend embracing Unitarian leader

indicators.note: something that embraces another wraps around it, so one piece goes inside
the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A gospel writer's companion hugs the head of a Unitarian church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evangelist's friend' looks like one phrase, but the 's is 'is', linking the definition Evangelist to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Paul was Christianity's great missionary preacher, an evangelist spreading the gospel.

clue.text: Snow crystal is source of frigid body of water

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

parts.note: a lake is an inland body of water

explanation.surface: A scientific claim that snow crystals come from an icy lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowflake is a single ice crystal, or a cluster of them, falling as snow.

clue.text: Expressive person, back at the front, becomes aloof

indicators.note: what is at the back of the word moves round to stand at its front

parts.note: an emoter is someone who shows feelings theatrically

explanation.surface: A gushing performer turns cold once pushed into the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of EMOTER moves to the start to give REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone remote is distant and unforthcoming in manner, standoffish.

clue.text: Blast it, the outside disappeared like the previous century

indicators.note: outside says these letters go round the next piece
a blast blows things apart, so the following letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A curse that the old facade has vanished, gone the way of the last century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast it' reads as an oath; Blast is the anagram signal for the next two words. The puzzle appeared in 2013, so the previous century was the 1900s.
explanation.definitionFit: The previous century, viewed from the 2000s, is the twentieth, the 1900s.

clue.text: Spooner's point: flowers kiss on the tundra

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds trade places

parts.note: a nub is a point or crux; its opening N trades places with the R of the flowers
roses are flowers; their opening R trades places with the N of the point

explanation.surface: A pointer that flowers can kiss, even out on the frozen plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of NUB ROSES gives RUB NOSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing noses is the popular picture of an Arctic peoples' greeting, the so-called Eskimo kiss.

clue.text: Free trip is cut short

indicators.note: a word that is cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a ride is a trip in a vehicle

explanation.surface: A complimentary excursion gets curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free trip' reads as one phrase; Free is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of something is to free or clear it of that thing.

clue.text: Farmer reorganized debts (ours)

indicators.note: something reorganized is put in a new order, as these letters are

explanation.surface: A farmer restructuring the loans the family owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodbuster is American slang for a farmer, especially one who ploughed the prairie grassland.

clue.text: Drop a third of two vowels

indicators.note: only the first third of the word is kept, the rest is discarded

parts.note: a diphthong is two vowel sounds glided together in one syllable

explanation.surface: Lose a third of a pair of vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine-letter word for two vowels is DIPHTHONG; its first three letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a drop, as in a dip in prices or in the road.

clue.text: Unfortunately, I trusted in leftovers

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is things going awry, so these letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having trusted the remains of last night's meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste, the remnants left behind.

clue.text: Chose to surround establishment's entrance and exit!

definitions.text: Chose to surround establishment's entrance and exit

indicators.note: surrounding something means going round it, so one piece goes outside the other
a word's entrance and exit are where it begins and ends

explanation.surface: Striking workers decided to block a business's way in and way out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of strikers at the gates, so there is no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikers who picketed a workplace stood at its gates to deter people going in or out.

clue.text: Run to sell drugs, covering the tip of Brooklyn and Long Island

indicators.note: what covers something goes around it, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: to push drugs is to sell them

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for Long Island

explanation.surface: A dealer's drug run that stretches across Brooklyn and Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' sounds like a dealer's errand; it is the definition, in its newspaper sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper that runs a story publishes it, printing it for readers.

clue.text: Commercial interrupting program's darkness

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a show is a television program

explanation.surface: An advert breaking into a broadcast that is all gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadow is the shade or darkness cast where light is blocked.

clue.text: Where rabbits are goin' at it, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the answer matches a phrase in sound rather than in spelling

parts.note: fighting one another is warring, said with the dropped g the clue imitates

explanation.surface: Rabbits, famous breeders, are busy at it in their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goin' at it' suggests rabbits breeding; read it instead as fighting, warrin' in casual speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is the network of burrows where a colony of rabbits lives.

clue.text: Hold on after lens cracked

indicators.note: after says the first piece follows the second
something cracked is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keep still while the camera glass is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening two words read as a request to wait; only the first word is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling hold, the arm locked under an opponent's arm and behind the neck.

clue.text: Dull reefer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cigar hollowed out and filled with marijuana

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a stoned smoker; a reefer is a marijuana cigarette, and its slang cousin is a cigar refilled with the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lacking an edge, and in slang a cannabis-filled cigar, so both senses give it.

clue.text: One grabbing a piece of food is inappropriate

indicators.note: what grabs something holds it within its grip
only a piece of the next word is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Snatching a snack is bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means unsuitable for a purpose, not appropriate.

clue.text: Ruminant returns for grass

indicators.note: something that returns heads back the way it came, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: deer chew the cud, so they are ruminants

explanation.surface: A grazing animal comes back to feed on grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass that grows in marshes and wet ground.

clue.text: What you'd hear in Edinburgh: "It's cold around the second of June"

indicators.note: around says the outer piece goes round the next one

parts.note: brr is what people say when they feel cold

indicators.note: only the letter in second position is taken

explanation.surface: A Scot's complaint about a chilly midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland. 'It's cold' looks like the quoted speech; it is the exclamation BRR.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is the rolled R of Scottish speech, the accent heard in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Merely fair

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a mediocre grade; the two words are separate senses of one adverb-adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adverb meaning only and an adjective meaning equitable, as a just verdict is.

clue.text: Superlatively doubtful counterfeit fifties

indicators.note: a counterfeit is a fake version, so these letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Fake fifty-dollar bills are the most suspect of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dubious; the -est form makes it the most doubtful.

clue.text: Go back and forth with criminal hustle: smuggling loot, ultimately

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden inside
something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
ultimately points to the very last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crook's scam: ferrying stolen goods to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuttle is to travel to and fro repeatedly between two places.

clue.text: Emerge from an egg or narrow door

definitions.meaning: first meaning: break out of the shell as a chick
second meaning: a small door or opening, as in a ship's deck

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a verb for a chick breaking out and a noun for a small opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a chick breaking out of its shell, and a small door or opening.

clue.text: Treason's unacceptable for government figures, 13 of whom appear in the completed grid

definitions.text: government figures, 13 of whom appear in the completed grid

indicators.note: what is unacceptable must be redone, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, including the s

explanation.surface: Betrayal is beyond the pale for elected lawmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid holds thirteen US senators of 2013: SESSIONS, COATS, KING, PAUL, FLAKE, BLUNT, REED, BURR, HATCH, SANDERS, CORKER, WARREN and NELSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Senators are elected members of the US Senate, the upper chamber of Congress.
